compiled_state.title: [CI/llm-review]: Provenance-aware dispatch skips review for sub-agent code that was never reviewed
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

The llm-review CI step's provenance-aware dispatch (`llm-review-dispatch-or-skip.sh`) incorrectly skips LLM review for sub-agent-authored code. PRs #401-405 (epic 3e36 field parity implementation — binding store, ADF walker, comment binding, outbound/inbound differs, reconcile check, sync logger) all showed `llm-review=pass` with `0 findings`, but investigation revealed the LLM was NEVER INVOKED. The code was authored by sub-agents in tracked Claude Code sessions, which gave the commits session provenance. The dispatch script treated this as "already reviewed by sub-PR" and wrote `{"findings":[], "skip_reason":"all_commits_provenanced"}`.

## Root cause

The provenance verifier (`verify-session-provenance.sh`) classifies commits as "covered" if they have session provenance (authored in a tracked Claude Code session). The dispatch script then skips LLM review for covered commits, assuming they were already reviewed in a sub-PR.

This assumption is WRONG for sub-agent-authored PRs:
- Sub-agent commits have session provenance (they ran in a Claude Code session) ✅
- Sub-agent commits were NEVER submitted to llm-review ❌
- The skip treats "known authorship" as "already reviewed" — conflating identity with review status

The correct skip criterion: a commit should only skip llm-review if it was part of a PR that PREVIOUSLY PASSED llm-review (the review has already run and produced findings). Session provenance alone is not sufficient — it means "we know who wrote this" not "we've already reviewed this."

## Impact

5 PRs merged without LLM review:
- PR #401: binding_store.py (14 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #402: adf.py + comment_binding.py (42 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #403: acli-integration.py field parity (115 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #404: outbound_differ.py + inbound_differ.py (14 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #405: reconcile_check.py + sync_logger.py (13 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED

Combined: ~700 new lines of production code + ~1200 lines of tests shipped without independent LLM review.

## Proposed fix

Change the skip criterion from "commit has session provenance" to "commit was part of a PR that passed llm-review." Specifically:

1. The provenance verifier should record not just "this commit has a session" but "this commit's session-PR passed llm-review"
2. The dispatch script's "covered" classification should require BOTH: (a) session provenance AND (b) the session-PR's llm-review check concluded=success with at least one finding evaluated (not a stub skip)
3. Sub-agent worktree PRs that go directly to main without a prior review cycle should be treated as unprovenanced (requiring full LLM review)

## Workaround

Until the fix ships, sub-agent PRs should be flagged for mandatory review. Options:
- Add a `force-review` label that overrides the provenance skip
- Check if the PR branch was created by a sub-agent (worktree branch naming convention) and force dispatch
